title: How fast do bacteria multiply?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why should leftovers be cooled quickly?

explain.say: Bacteria multiply by splitting in two. One becomes two, two become four, four become eight. This doubling makes their numbers explode faster than you might believe.
In ideal conditions some bacteria divide every 20 minutes. Each cell grows, copies its DNA and splits down the middle into two identical cells. This is called binary fission.
Three doublings an hour means 8 cells after one hour and about 4,000 after four hours. After eight hours one cell could become over 16 million, which is why food left out warm becomes risky so fast.
In real life the doubling cannot go on forever. The bacteria run out of food and space and are poisoned by their own waste, so growth slows, levels off and eventually the numbers fall.

faq.a: By binary fission: a bacterium grows, copies its single loop of DNA and pinches in the middle to make two identical daughter cells. No partner is needed.
Some, like E. coli in a warm laboratory broth, can divide about every 20 minutes. Others are much slower; the bacterium that causes tuberculosis takes around 15 to 20 hours.

faq.q: Why don't bacteria cover the whole Earth?
faq.a: Because their food, space and water run out, their waste builds up, and other living things eat them. Growth always levels off long before it gets out of hand.
Exponential growth is when something keeps multiplying by the same amount in equal times, like doubling every 20 minutes. It starts slowly, then shoots up incredibly fast.

faq.q: Why do leftovers need to be cooled quickly?
faq.a: Warm food lets bacteria double over and over. Cooling leftovers within a couple of hours and keeping them in the fridge stops a few bacteria becoming millions.
